## Summary

Bind NCCL EP handles in JAX via `ncclEpImportHandle` so handle memory is owned by the caller instead of the pointer-keyed cache, which breaks when XLA relocates `handle_mem` (e.g. under `lax.scan`). PyTorch keeps its handle cache.

## Implementation

- Add `nvte_ep_*_v2` per-step ops taking an explicit `NVTEEpLayerConfig` (new `topk_idx_dtype` field) that rebind a handle from `handle_mem` on every call.
- `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=0` now disables the cache; the JAX extension sets it and uses only the `_v2` ops.
- Export `handle_mem` from the JAX prepare primitive; error at the live-handle cap instead of evicting.
- Default JAX `topk_idx` to int32 and validate it at prepare.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[High impact]** No new reportable blockers were found beyond the existing review threads.

Summary

JAX now rebuilds EP handles from caller-owned `handle_mem` through `ncclEpImportHandle`. - JAX rebuilds EP handles from each step’s saved routing data. - A zero cache limit disables EP handle caching. - JAX EP configs now carry the routing-index data type. The previous and current commits have different merge bases with the target commit, so this review used the full PR diff. All supplied previous threads are unnumbered and therefore have no `previousFindings` entries.

Diagram

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR A[JAX prepare] --> B[Caller-owned handle_mem] B --> C[XLA may move the buffer] C --> D[Per-step v2 call with layer config] D --> E[ncclEpImportHandle] E --> F[Dispatch, combine, or backward] F --> G[Destroy temporary host handle] ``` Reviews (10) · Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into ep\_import\_handl..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/09bb745214043b25051ddcfc9193a861eda5012b) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_expert&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=code_reviews&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Default dtype mismatches saved routing** `EpLayerConfig` now defaults `topk_idx_dtype` to int64, but existing callers in `ep_moe.py` and `ep_bench.py` use int32 indices without setting this field. Prepare uses the tensor's actual dtype. Later calls import the saved state as int64, so dispatch, combine, and backward receive a handle that does not match the prepared routing. Derive the dtype from `topk_idx` and preserve it for later calls, or update callers and reject mismatched configs before prepare. **Knowledge Base Used:** [JAX distributed and MoE execution](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/jax-distributed-moe.md)

-    Threaded through every per-step op so the pointer-keyed C++ cache can

+    dispatch_bwd, and combine_bwd don't otherwise see topk_idx directly.

nodes.body: **Eviction restores an old dtype** `prepare_handle_locked` treats configs with different `topk_idx_dtype` values as equal and returns without refreshing the saved config. If a buffer is prepared with int32 indices and later with int64 indices at the same address, its saved dtype remains int32. After eviction, the new recovery path imports the current routing state with that old dtype, rebuilding a handle that does not match the latest prepare. Include the dtype in `same_cfg`, or refresh the saved config after a successful prepare. **Knowledge Base Used:** [Native CUDA kernel platform](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/native-kernels.md)

**Freed buffers leave cache entries** Every eviction now keeps a `HandleEntry` in `evicted_`, but that map has no limit or buffer-release cleanup. Entries disappear only when the address is used again or the whole backend shuts down. Long-lived callers that prepare buffers at new addresses retain metadata for freed buffers indefinitely, so `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE` no longer bounds the cache's host memory. Tie this metadata to buffer lifetime or provide an explicit release path.

**Mixed test modes fail late** The newly selectable `TestEpScanHandleRelocation` uses self-hosted communication, but `_ep_test_cases` does not include it in the check that forbids mixing communication modes. Selecting it with `TestEPBorrowedComm` passes this check and later fails during bootstrap because changing modes requires a new process. Add the new class to the check, preferably by using each class's `USE_BORROWED_COMM` setting.

**Freed buffers exhaust the cache** `prepare_handle_locked` now stops at the cache limit, but freeing an `EpBuffer` never removes its entry. If a PyTorch caller prepares buffers at enough different addresses, it hits `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE` even after earlier buffers were freed. Valid EP calls then fail until the backend shuts down or the limit is raised. Add a per-buffer release path, or stop counting released buffers against the live-handle limit.

Not changing. The cap bounds distinct live `handle_mem` buffers, and a program needs one per layer per in-flight microbatch (e.g. 61 layers x PP degree for DeepSeek-V3), far below the 4096 default. Buffers are meant to be reused across steps; `ep_finalize` clears the cache, and
  `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE` can be raised if needed.

Understood. Given the intended lifecycle—buffers are reused across steps, `ep_finalize` clears the cache, and the default capacity of 4096 is well above the expected per-process working set—I agree this is an accepted capacity trade-off rather than a blocker for this PR.

Strictly speaking, the cache retains entries after the underlying buffer is freed, so the cap bounds cached addresses rather than provably live buffers; address churn could still consume the limit. I’ll leave the comment as non-actionable based on the stated usage model.

Tip: You can customize Greptile's behavior for this repo with [`.greptile/rules.md` and `.greptile/config.json`](https://www.greptile.com/docs/code-review/custom-standards).

**JAX disables PyTorch EP** `MakeEpGroupConfig` sets `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=0` for the whole process, not just JAX. If a program runs JAX EP, fully shuts it down, then starts PyTorch EP in the same process, PyTorch inherits the disabled cache. Its non-`_v2` calls, including `nvte_ep_combine`, then fail with “EP op without layer_cfg requires the handle cache.” The per-device backend keeps its saved cache size after shutdown, so restoring the environment alone does not fix this. Keep JAX’s cache choice local to its EP group instead of overwriting the process setting.

**Borrowed EP keeps caching handles** Disabling the cache in `EpResources` misses borrowed-communicator bootstrap. That path calls `nvte_ep_initialize` directly, so removing `disable_handle_cache` leaves JAX prepare calls using the pointer cache. If `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=1`, preparing two distinct routing buffers now fails. With the default limit, 4096 distinct prepared addresses exhaust the cache, and later EP calls fail until shutdown. Disable the cache for both JAX bootstrap paths, preferably through a group-local setting. **Knowledge Base Used:** [JAX runtime and public API](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/jax-runtime.md)

+# lax.scan handle_mem relocation

+class TestEpScanHandleRelocation(TestEP):
+    """Regression test for handle_mem address relocation under ``lax.scan``.
+
+    XLA may reuse the same ``handle_mem`` address for a different prepared
+    routing state at each forward step, and independently restore each
+    backward step's saved state at its own address. EPBackend never caches
+    handles by address for JAX (the JAX extension sets
+    ``NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=0``, disabling the handle cache): every
+    dispatch/combine/_bwd call rebinds a fresh handle from
+    ``handle_mem``'s own contents via ``ncclEpImportHandle``, so the address
+    is irrelevant.
+
+    Runs several EP-MoE-style layers, each with a different per-layer routing
+    pattern so consecutive scan steps genuinely prepare distinct state, via
+    ``lax.scan`` and cross-checks against the same computation unrolled as a
+    plain Python loop (no loop-carried buffer for XLA to alias). If handle
+    binding ever breaks again, the two diverge or the scanned path errors.
+    """
+
+    NUM_LAYERS = 3
+
+    def _make_layered_inputs(self):
+        """Per-layer routing that differs across layers/steps, so consecutive
+        scan steps genuinely prepare distinct handle_mem state (the condition
+        under which stale/misattributed handle reuse would be visible)."""
+        T_global = TOKENS_PER_DP_SHARD * self.dp
+        E = self.num_experts
+        idx = np.empty((self.NUM_LAYERS, T_global, TOP_K), dtype=np.int32)
+        for layer in range(self.NUM_LAYERS):
+            for t in range(T_global):
+                for k in range(TOP_K):
+                    idx[layer, t, k] = (t * TOP_K + k + layer * 7) % E
+        topk_idx_stack = jnp.asarray(idx)
+        topk_weights = jnp.full((T_global, TOP_K), 1.0 / TOP_K, dtype=jnp.float32)
+        tokens = jnp.asarray(
+            np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, T_global * HIDDEN_DIM, dtype=np.float32).reshape(
+                T_global, HIDDEN_DIM
+            ),
+            dtype=jnp.bfloat16,
+        )
+        return T_global, topk_idx_stack, tokens, topk_weights
+
+    def _layer_step(self, dp_spec, ep_spec_3d, ep_spec_2d, T_global, tokens, topk_idx_layer, w):
+        """One EP-MoE-style layer: dispatch, an identity "expert" (the round
+        trip itself), and combine. Returns the combined output, which a
+        deterministic routing with per-token top-k weights summing to 1
+        recovers as ``tokens`` regardless of which experts were chosen."""
+        tokens = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(tokens, NamedSharding(self.mesh, dp_spec))
+        topk_idx_layer = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(
+            topk_idx_layer, NamedSharding(self.mesh, dp_spec)
+        )
+        w = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(w, NamedSharding(self.mesh, dp_spec))
+        recv_t, recv_w, hm, tc, _trt = ep_dispatch(
+            self.hk, topk_idx_layer, tokens, w, self.recv_capacity_per_rank
+        )
+        recv_t = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(recv_t, NamedSharding(self.mesh, ep_spec_3d))
+        recv_w = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(recv_w, NamedSharding(self.mesh, ep_spec_2d))
+        weighted = self._preweight_expert_out(recv_t, recv_w)
+        out = ep_combine(self.hk, hm, tc, weighted, T_global, out_sharding=(("dp", "ep"), None))
+        return jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(out, NamedSharding(self.mesh, dp_spec))
+
+    def test_scan_matches_unrolled_forward(self):
+        """lax.scan over layers with distinct per-step routing == the unrolled loop."""
+        T_global, topk_idx_stack, tokens, topk_w = self._make_layered_inputs()
+        dp_spec = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None)
+        ep_spec_3d = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None, None)
+        ep_spec_2d = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None)
+
+        with self.mesh, global_shard_guard(self.mr):
+
+            def step(carry, idx_layer):
+                out = self._layer_step(
+                    dp_spec, ep_spec_3d, ep_spec_2d, T_global, carry, idx_layer, topk_w
+                )
+                return out, None
+
+            @jax.jit
+            def scanned(toks, idx_stack):
+                final, _ = jax.lax.scan(step, toks, idx_stack)
+                return final
+
+            @jax.jit
+            def unrolled(toks, idx_stack):
+                carry = toks
+                # Plain Python loop: fully unrolled at trace time, no
+                # loop-carried buffer for XLA to alias across "steps".
+                for layer in range(self.NUM_LAYERS):
+                    carry, _ = step(carry, idx_stack[layer])
+                return carry
+
+            out_scan = scanned(tokens, topk_idx_stack)
+            out_unroll = unrolled(tokens, topk_idx_stack)
+            out_scan.block_until_ready()
+            out_unroll.block_until_ready()
+            scan_g = jmu.process_allgather(out_scan, tiled=True)
+            unroll_g = jmu.process_allgather(out_unroll, tiled=True)
+
+        if self.rank == 0:
+            # Primary regression signal: scan and unrolled run the identical
+            # math with different XLA buffer scheduling -- they must agree.
+            np.testing.assert_allclose(
+                np.asarray(scan_g.astype(jnp.float32)),
+                np.asarray(unroll_g.astype(jnp.float32)),
+                atol=5e-2,
+                rtol=5e-2,
+            )
+            # Secondary sanity check: N identity-routing layers recover tokens.
+            np.testing.assert_allclose(
+                np.asarray(scan_g.astype(jnp.float32)),
+                np.asarray(tokens.astype(jnp.float32)),
+                atol=5e-2,
+                rtol=5e-2,
+            )
+
+    def test_scan_matches_unrolled_backward(self):
+        """Gradients through lax.scan (fwd+bwd relocation) == the unrolled loop.
+
+        Each scan step's backward re-imports handle_mem at whatever address
+        XLA restored that step's saved (forward) state to, which may differ
+        from the forward address and from every other step's.
+        """
+        T_global, topk_idx_stack, tokens, topk_w = self._make_layered_inputs()
+        dp_spec = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None)
+        ep_spec_3d = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None, None)
+        ep_spec_2d = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None)
+
+        with self.mesh, global_shard_guard(self.mr):
+
+            def step(carry, idx_layer):
+                out = self._layer_step(
+                    dp_spec, ep_spec_3d, ep_spec_2d, T_global, carry, idx_layer, topk_w
+                )
+                return out, None
+
+            def loss_scan(toks, idx_stack):
+                final, _ = jax.lax.scan(step, toks, idx_stack)
+                return 0.5 * (final.astype(jnp.float32) ** 2).sum()
+
+            def loss_unrolled(toks, idx_stack):
+                carry = toks
+                for layer in range(self.NUM_LAYERS):
+                    carry, _ = step(carry, idx_stack[layer])
+                return 0.5 * (carry.astype(jnp.float32) ** 2).sum()

+        for layer in range(self.NUM_LAYERS):

+        """EP layer whose expert scales its input by a factor that depends on the
+        destination ep rank, so the output changes if routing state is misattributed."""
+        dp_spec = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None)
+        ep_spec_3d = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None, None)
+        ep_spec_2d = PartitionSpec(("dp", "ep"), None)

+        x = np.asarray(tokens.astype(jnp.float32))
+        coefs = []

+            coef = (w_stack[layer] * scale).sum(-1)
+            coefs.append(coef)
+            x = x * coef[:, None]
+        return x, np.prod(coefs, axis=0)

+        """lax.scan (no jax.checkpoint, so handle_mem is a saved residual) forward and

inline_comments.body: **Eviction restores an old dtype** `prepare_handle_locked` treats configs with different `topk_idx_dtype` values as equal and returns without refreshing the saved config. If a buffer is prepared with int32 indices and later with int64 indices at the same address, its saved dtype remains int32. After eviction, the new recovery path imports the current routing state with that old dtype, rebuilding a handle that does not match the latest prepare. Include the dtype in `same_cfg`, or refresh the saved config after a successful prepare. **Knowledge Base Used:** [Native CUDA kernel platform](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/native-kernels.md)

**Freed buffers leave cache entries** Every eviction now keeps a `HandleEntry` in `evicted_`, but that map has no limit or buffer-release cleanup. Entries disappear only when the address is used again or the whole backend shuts down. Long-lived callers that prepare buffers at new addresses retain metadata for freed buffers indefinitely, so `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE` no longer bounds the cache's host memory. Tie this metadata to buffer lifetime or provide an explicit release path.

**Mixed test modes fail late** The newly selectable `TestEpScanHandleRelocation` uses self-hosted communication, but `_ep_test_cases` does not include it in the check that forbids mixing communication modes. Selecting it with `TestEPBorrowedComm` passes this check and later fails during bootstrap because changing modes requires a new process. Add the new class to the check, preferably by using each class's `USE_BORROWED_COMM` setting.

**Freed buffers exhaust the cache** `prepare_handle_locked` now stops at the cache limit, but freeing an `EpBuffer` never removes its entry. If a PyTorch caller prepares buffers at enough different addresses, it hits `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE` even after earlier buffers were freed. Valid EP calls then fail until the backend shuts down or the limit is raised. Add a per-buffer release path, or stop counting released buffers against the live-handle limit.

Not changing. The cap bounds distinct live `handle_mem` buffers, and a program needs one per layer per in-flight microbatch (e.g. 61 layers x PP degree for DeepSeek-V3), far below the 4096 default. Buffers are meant to be reused across steps; `ep_finalize` clears the cache, and
  `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE` can be raised if needed.

Understood. Given the intended lifecycle—buffers are reused across steps, `ep_finalize` clears the cache, and the default capacity of 4096 is well above the expected per-process working set—I agree this is an accepted capacity trade-off rather than a blocker for this PR.

Strictly speaking, the cache retains entries after the underlying buffer is freed, so the cap bounds cached addresses rather than provably live buffers; address churn could still consume the limit. I’ll leave the comment as non-actionable based on the stated usage model.

Tip: You can customize Greptile's behavior for this repo with [`.greptile/rules.md` and `.greptile/config.json`](https://www.greptile.com/docs/code-review/custom-standards).

**JAX disables PyTorch EP** `MakeEpGroupConfig` sets `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=0` for the whole process, not just JAX. If a program runs JAX EP, fully shuts it down, then starts PyTorch EP in the same process, PyTorch inherits the disabled cache. Its non-`_v2` calls, including `nvte_ep_combine`, then fail with “EP op without layer_cfg requires the handle cache.” The per-device backend keeps its saved cache size after shutdown, so restoring the environment alone does not fix this. Keep JAX’s cache choice local to its EP group instead of overwriting the process setting.

**Borrowed EP keeps caching handles** Disabling the cache in `EpResources` misses borrowed-communicator bootstrap. That path calls `nvte_ep_initialize` directly, so removing `disable_handle_cache` leaves JAX prepare calls using the pointer cache. If `NVTE_EP_HANDLE_CACHE_SIZE=1`, preparing two distinct routing buffers now fails. With the default limit, 4096 distinct prepared addresses exhaust the cache, and later EP calls fail until shutdown. Disable the cache for both JAX bootstrap paths, preferably through a group-local setting. **Knowledge Base Used:** [JAX runtime and public API](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/jax-runtime.md)

**[High impact]** No new reportable blockers were found beyond the existing review threads.

Summary

JAX now rebuilds EP handles from caller-owned `handle_mem` through `ncclEpImportHandle`. - JAX rebuilds EP handles from each step’s saved routing data. - A zero cache limit disables EP handle caching. - JAX EP configs now carry the routing-index data type. The previous and current commits have different merge bases with the target commit, so this review used the full PR diff. All supplied previous threads are unnumbered and therefore have no `previousFindings` entries.
